old: Its first sound didn't originally belong to it — it wandered over from the little word beside it.
It once began with an 'n,' back when it meant a small tablecloth.
Like 'adder' and 'newt,' it lost a letter to the article 'a' standing next to it.
clues: This piece of clothing lost its original first letter when speakers misheard it after 'a' and moved the n onto the article instead.
Tied over your front at the waist, it keeps clothes clean while you cook; unlike a smock, it is sleeveless and open at the back. Its ancestor meant 'little tablecloth.'
Someone overly dependent on their mother is said to be tied to her ___ strings, and the paved area where planes park at an airport shares the name.
